rows.grounds: compound of bhāskara-ācaraṇa (Bhāskarācāra/feet) and ādhārā (support, foundation); feminine epithet
compound of bhāskara-ācaraṇa (Bhāskarācāra/feet) and āśritā (resorted-to, sheltered-by); feminine epithet

items.question: In what manner is the goddess grounded in and devoted to Bhāskarācāra's feet?
premises: The goddess is characterized as having Bhāskarācāra's feet as her support.
The goddess is characterized as resorting to Bhāskarācāra's feet.
Both epithets express a foundational dependence and refuge in Bhāskarācāra's feet.
items.inference: The goddess is presented as both established upon and taking refuge in Bhāskarācāra's feet.
uncertainties: Whether bhāskarācāraṇa refers specifically to the feet of Bhāskarācāra as a person or carries an additional symbolic sense is not fully determined by this verse alone.
items.plain_english: She is supported by Bhāskarācāra's feet and takes refuge in Bhāskarācāra's feet.
